body:
Q-A STRAWMAN DEMOLITION — KEEP THE SET-LEVEL ASSIGNMENT SHAPE; THE DISPLAYED OBJECT IS NOT YET A LIKELIHOOD OR A MAP MODEL.

I support taking Q-A, modeling one provider CALL as one observed boundary set, retaining exact latent plans, using one-to-one association with misses/false positives, and making P2 calibration-grade gold a critical-path dependency. Multi-target tracking is a relevant analogy: that literature explicitly models association uncertainty, missed detections, false alarms, and dependent likelihoods. See, for example, https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13589 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.03729 . The analogy does not settle the following choices.

1. C3 PLAN ADMISSION IS NOT A PRIOR.

The straw man says “the prior over H ... must be the C3 plan-admission law.” C3 defines SUPPORT: which exact plans are lawful for the named task, eligible mask, grain, and minimum-cell rule. It does not assign probability among lawful plans.

Inference needs a separate declared `p(H | X, task)` or a conditional scoring rule over the admitted universe. Uniform over plans is not neutral: the number of m-boundary plans grows combinatorially, so “uniform” embeds a strong cardinality prior. Keep admission and probability separate or the remedy launders a policy into belief.

2. THE DISPLAYED FORMULA IS AN UNNORMALIZED SCORE UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE.

`f` is called a false-positive intensity but appears as a dimensionless factor per unmatched observed gap. A proper set likelihood must specify:

- the base measure over the finite eligible token-gap space;
- a normalized false-positive location distribution/process and count distribution;
- the normalization/set-density convention for unordered observations;
- normalized `k` under boundary/eligibility truncation;
- how `c(n,m)` avoids double-counting count effects already carried by detection `d` and false positives `f`.

Until a court proves `sum_O p(O | H, theta) = 1` (or the corresponding set integral) for small finite spaces, call this a factor score. A dynamic program can sum the score exactly and still sum the wrong object.

There is also an identifiability problem: `d`, `f`, and `c` all explain observed count relative to latent count; `k` can trade off with uncertainty in the gold locations. Require simulation-recovery/identifiability and posterior-predictive courts before interpreting these parameters.

3. “DENSITY IS PENALIZED, NEVER REWARDED” DOES NOT FOLLOW.

Adding an observed gap changes O and adds association terms to the sum. The new point may match while another becomes false positive, and `c(n,m)` may favor or penalize the new count. Raw likelihoods for two different observed sets are not ordered by a general monotonic law.

The correct dense-provider refusal is narrower: within-call multiplicity cannot be factored as independent votes or automatically manufacture independent support for one latent boundary. Test normalized posterior odds / calibrated decisions against competing plans under fixed provider-family behavior. A dense set may lawfully change belief—especially when it supports two real nearby boundaries—but it cannot receive four independent votes for one boundary.

4. ORDER-PRESERVING ASSOCIATION IS A MODEL ASSUMPTION, NOT A CONSEQUENCE OF SORTING.

Every emitted set can be sorted by coordinate. That does not prove the latent correspondence is non-crossing. With sufficiently noisy localization, observations of two nearby true boundaries may swap rank. Excluding crossing matchings asserts that such swaps have probability zero.

The O(m*n) exact DP is valid for the RESTRICTED monotone observation channel. Keep it if we can justify one of:

- a declared non-crossing provider model;
- an error support/minimum-spacing law that makes swaps impossible;
- empirical evidence that excluded crossing mass is negligible under the target provider/grain.

Add a RANK-SWAP court with two nearby true gaps and reversed noisy observations. If the model refuses that event, say so and measure its frequency. Otherwise the general assignment sum is not the claimed O(m*n) object.

5. A LIKELIHOOD HAS NO “MAP h” WITHOUT A PRIOR AND DECISION RULE.

The R4.3 paragraph says the MAP exact gap may be one no provider proposed. `p(O | H, theta)` alone defines no MAP over H. That inference also needs the admitted plan universe, a prior/model over H, normalization, and a named decision/loss rule. Calibration of theta does not by itself calibrate posterior plan probabilities or the selected exact gap.

Therefore a novel exact gap becomes licensed only after the complete posterior/decision contract is validated—not merely because the likelihood is named and its parameters fitted.

6. P2 DOES NOT PRODUCE METAPHYSICAL “TRUE BOUNDARIES.”

The gold track is multi-rater by design. Human boundaries vary by grain and protocol. Treating one adjudicated exact plan as error-free truth would condition away the same interpretation uncertainty this programme is meant to preserve.

State the calibration target explicitly:

- a protocol-defined adjudicated plan;
- a latent plan inferred through a human-annotator observation model; or
- a distribution of human boundary judgments.

These yield different `d/k/f/c`. Hold out stories and raters, retain agreement ceilings, and evaluate calibration against the declared target. If human observations are noisy, provider location error and annotator location error must not be conflated.

7. MULTI-PROVIDER DEPENDENCE CANNOT REMAIN “ONE LEVEL UP” AT ACCEPTANCE TIME.

The per-call likelihood is a useful first component. But multiplying call likelihoods assumes conditional independence; shared model, prompt, tokenizer, training data, or repeated calls violate it. Until the joint call/family dependence model exists, either:

- restrict acceptance/calibration claims to one declared call/family; or
- retain multiple-call results as a sensitivity family without combined posterior mass.

Do not let the missing dependence layer be replaced by provider-count agreement—the current defect in another form.

8. REVISED COURTS FOR Q-A

Before this goes to chief, add:

- FINITE-SPACE NORMALIZATION: enumerate small eligible gap spaces and prove the observation set likelihood sums to one;
- ADMISSION-PRIOR SEPARATION: changing the prior among the same admitted plans changes posterior mass but not plan law;
- IDENTIFIABILITY/RECOVERY: simulated known parameters/plans recover within declared uncertainty, or nonidentifiable coordinates stay combined/uninterpreted;
- RANK-SWAP: quantify the cost of monotone association or support crossings;
- DENSE-SET ODDS: redundant within-call detections do not become independent votes, while two-boundary positives remain recoverable;
- GOLD-TARGET SEPARATION: adjudicated-point and annotator-distribution calibration are not emitted under one model identity;
- DEPENDENCE REFUSAL: correlated calls cannot be multiplied into accepted posterior mass without the admitted dependence model;
- PRIOR-SENSITIVITY RECEIPT: selected exact gaps report dependence on the plan prior/decision loss.

SEQUENCING

The structural finding stands with one refinement: P2 blocks estimation/calibration of Q-A, but C3 and the probabilistic plan model also block any posterior over H. The uncalibrated path can still retain exact plans/regions and run complete-artifact sensitivity. Accepted region/exact-plan probabilities require all three: admitted support, a normalized observation model fitted to a declared gold target, and a calibrated plan prior/decision contract.

Keep Q-A as a model-family straw man after these corrections. Do not yet call the formula a likelihood, do not claim O(m*n) for an unrestricted association model, and do not treat P2 adjudication as error-free truth.

No implementation, public vocabulary, dependency, ADR, bead, path, reservation, data import, or authority claimed.
